title: Hopeverse identity: The Return v2 (grip kept through the middle)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

request.prompt: Dark modern Tamil mass-hero introduction film score with a unique signature sound built from broken, processed Carnatic instruments. 108 BPM half-time swagger, C sharp minor. Signature motif: a rising 3-note call (root, up a minor third, up to the fifth, the last note held and bent upward) on a gritty synth lead in the first 5 seconds and again at the end. The electronic layer is made of chopped and processed Carnatic sounds: a stuttering, glitch-chopped veena riff partners the synth lead; a mridangam pitched down and time-stretched becomes the deep bass hit; reversed, pitch-shifted nadaswaram phrases become the risers; ghatam and kanjira are cut into tight glitchy percussion. Underneath, a thick steady synth bass, deep cinematic drums and low brass and strings. Vocals: deep male crowd chants and wordless shouts like 'hey!' and 'ho!' answering the theme, no lyrics, no singer. Signature sound: a reversed veena swell rising into a big hit at every section change. 0-12 s: tease with the synth bass, a ticking glitched ghatam pulse, the 3-note call, stuttered veena fragments. 12-14 s: reversed veena swell, one huge hit, crowd 'hey!', the full theme. 14-34 s: the 4-bar theme on the synth lead with the chopped veena answering, chants between phrases. 34-36 s: a sudden one-bar drop to just the pitched mridangam bass hit and a crowd shout, then BANG back in. 36-44 s: the main hook returns with full drums at full power, a call-and-response chant ('hey!'... 'ho!') on every bar, the drums never thin out. 44-52 s: everything at full power with the brass and the pitched mridangam bass, a new rising brass counter-line on top. Something new happens at least every 8 seconds; the drum density never drops in the middle. 52-60 s: the theme one last time, a hard final hit, then the 3-note call rings out. No clean unprocessed Carnatic solos; no silence or long pauses, no side-chain pumping, no EDM drops; clear, tonal, punchy, very loud cinematic mix; no white-noise sweeps, no harsh fuzz.

brief.notes: Jithesh loved the first demo but it lost grip at 35-45 s (hits fell, nothing new for ~18 s). Rule 9.8: a new event every 8 s; hook returns at ~60%.

story: The hero walks back into his city, scored in our own signature sound.
